section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch12 — Individual Differences — Deep
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Two children of the same age and grade differ noticeably in their pace of learning, interests, learning styles, and emotional responses, even when taught by the same teacher in the same classroom. This variation among learners is called:
explanation: Individual differences refer to the natural variation among learners in ability, pace, interest, personality, and learning style — a normal phenomenon requiring differentiated teaching, not a disorder or delay.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch12 — Individual Differences — Deep
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Individual differences among learners arise from the interaction of two broad sources: inherited characteristics passed from parents, and the influence of upbringing, culture, and experiences. These two sources are respectively called:

options.option_text: Nature and Nurture — but only nurture matters in practice
Maturation only, with environment playing no role

explanation: Heredity (genetic inheritance) and Environment (upbringing, culture, experiences) interact to produce individual differences — modern developmental psychology treats this as a continuous interaction, not either factor alone.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch12 — Individual Differences — Deep
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Recognising that students in the same class have different readiness levels, interests, and learning profiles, and therefore adjusting content, process, or product accordingly, is the core idea behind:

options.option_text: Uniform instruction for all students identically

explanation: Differentiated instruction directly responds to individual differences by varying content, process, or product to match each learner's readiness, interest, and profile — a practical classroom application of this principle.
